To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) cadherins are essential for tissue morphogenesis and suppress invasion, (2) cadherins regulate the actin cytoskeleton and (3) cadherin-mediated cell-cell adhesion is regulated by a number of intracellular signals.
cadherins are the major determinants of tissue architecture and suppressors of invasiveness.

cadherins are involved in the regulation of cell-cell interactions, cell motility and cell growth, that they are regulated by extracellular signals and that they are involved in the control of cell differentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (i) the molecular and biochemical characterization of the cadherins, (ii) their role in the development of the nervous system, (iii) the regulation of cadherin expression, (iv) the molecular mechanism of cadherin mediated cell-cell adhesion, and (v) the role of cadherins in tumor invasion and metastasis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cadherins are important regulators of cell-cell interactions and tissue architecture, but that their exact functions in the different tissues and during the various stages of development are still poorly understood.
we have only just scratched the surface of the cadherins.
the molecular mechanisms by which cadherins regulate cell-cell adhesion, morphogenesis and suppress tumor invasion are still largely unknown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cadherins act as suppressors of invasion and that their loss is an important step in the metastatic cascade.
the cadherins are the major determinants of cell sorting in tissues, and that the cadherin/catenin complex is a major regulator of the cytoskeleton.
the cadherins are a large family of cell-cell adhesion proteins with diverse biological activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cadherin function is not restricted to cell-cell contacts, but also includes the regulation of cell motility.
cadherins are not only determinants of cell-cell adhesion but also suppressors of cell invasion and metastasis.
cadherins are more than mere glue.
